claims.text: An intermediate or optimal Fe doping level in Ni-based layered double hydroxides enhances oxygen-evolution activity relative to undoped Ni hydroxide.
An intermediate or optimal Fe doping level improves catalyst durability relative to undoped Ni hydroxide.
Both lower-than-optimal and excessive Fe contents produce poorer performance than the optimal Fe content.
The baseline material is hydrothermally synthesized Ni hydroxide LDH containing 0% Fe.
Fe incorporation changes the local electronic structure and e_g orbital occupancy at Ni sites.
Fe dopants alter the electronic environment of Ni centers.
Fe-induced electronic changes adjust the adsorption energies of oxygenated OER intermediates.
At optimal Fe content, the electronic structure favors faster charge transfer.
At optimal Fe content, oxygenated intermediates are stabilized in a way that promotes efficient oxygen evolution.
Too little Fe leads to suboptimal adsorption energies and poorer OER performance.
Excessive Fe can cause suboptimal adsorption energies or phase instability that decreases durability.
The optimally Fe-doped sample will require a lower overpotential at a fixed current density than pure Ni hydroxide.
The proposed trend applies under controlled hydrothermal synthesis, homogeneous Fe distribution, phase purity, and testing in 0.1–1 M KOH.
Changes in synthesis conditions or formation of phase impurities may limit applicability of the proposed Fe-content trend.
The optimal Fe content may vary with subtle synthesis parameters and the method used to characterize electronic structure.
Unintended secondary phases could confound the relationship between Fe content, electronic structure, and OER performance.
